h: A New Shabbos Table Draws the Spirit of Holiness

p: In the holy Zohar on this parashah (192a):
"'And you shall make a table, etc.' (Shemos 25:23),
'and you shall place on the table, etc.'
the Holy One, blessed be He, wanted
For the drawing down of the spirit from the supernal Holiness
is through the arranging of the table
And the table of the Shabbos meals
is like the table in the Mikdash,
I will place to the north,"
along the lines of what it says (Yoma 21b):
"the table in the north and the menorah in the south,"
which is the spreading of the shelter of peace over us,
in the aspect of the table that was in the Mikdash;
דְּאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קנד, ב)
for it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 154b):
every bit of food was blessed
דְּלָא לְקַטְרְגָא בְּהוּ יֵצֶר הָרַע וְכוּלֵּי
so that the yetzer hara not accuse through them, etc."
for it benefited all the eating of the Kohanim,
And likewise the eating of Shabbos benefits
And this is "to draw the holy spirit
שֶׁזֶּהוּ עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק
for this is through the middah of Yosef HaTzaddik,
who is the drawing down to the last middah,
the aspect of the holy Chakal Tapuchin.
(as it says in Midrash Rabbah, Chukas),
in heaven and on earth" (Divrei HaYamim I 29:11),
"which holds on to heaven and earth":
for he joins the middah of Tiferes
with the middah of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael.
And so we find regarding Yosef
that he fed the tribes a Shabbos meal,
for his power was to bring about
that the eating be in holiness;
and this is "to draw the holy spirit
And this is the meaning of "We invite her":
that is, the holiness of Chakal Tapuchin,
to draw the holy spirit from above.
And likewise it says there regarding Bilam
that he would arrange a table for the Other Side,
like a monkey after a man;
שֶׁבִּלְעָם גַּם כֵּן הָיָה מַזְכִּיר שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה
for Bilam too would mention the Name Havayah,
as a believer in the Name Havayah;
and he would arrange a table for the Other Side,
as it says in the holy Zohar.
And just as in holiness we invite
the aspect of "a field that Hashem has blessed,"
so in the kelipah he wished to draw down
through a table to the field;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קכב, א)
as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 122a):
in which all blessings and holiness rest,
'like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed';
in which all destruction and impurity,
And for this Bilam wished to draw down from above,
from the head of the kelipah,
through a table for the Other Side.
And as for our saying "with a new table"
כִּי בְּכָל שַׁבָּת יֵשׁ קְדוּשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה
for on every Shabbos there is a new holiness,
since it is called a bride,
and a bride is only seven days;
which implies that on every Shabbos
"Let the earth bring forth living souls":
"the earth" is the middah of Malchus,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג לט, ב)
as it says (in the holy Zohar, Zohar III 39b);
and likewise the spirit is from there,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קנז, א)
as it says (in the holy Zohar, Zohar II 157a):
"'And the advantage of the land is in everything'
is a spirit to this body";
we call it the Oral Torah";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קפח, ב)
and as it says in the holy Zohar (this parashah, 188b):
but in it there is ches-tes,
That is, it has in it the letters ches-tes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ
as the holy Zohar says afterward;
that is, the kelipah of Esav,
"and the house of Esav for straw,"
and chaff is the kelipah of Yishmael.
"and a wind passed and cleansed them":
for purity is the opposite of the kelipah of Yishmael,
וְרוּחַ הַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and "wind" is the aspect of the Oral Torah,
which is a spirit from the Holiness on High
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סא, א)
"For in much wisdom is much anger":
שֶׁהָרַב חָכְמָה בָּא לְתַקֵּן הָרַב כַּעַס
for "much wisdom" comes to repair "much anger."
And this is the letter hei in "chitah,"
which indicates the middah of Malchus,
the sum of the twenty-two letters,"
as it says in the holy Zohar.
That is, as the first light was
when everything was included in the Written Torah:
corresponding to the five books of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג
as it says in Bereishis Rabbah 3;
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah"
that is, everything was included in them;
and then the utterance "Let there be light"
was the second utterance, which is Chochmah,
that is, that there is recognition and grasp in it.
אַךְ לְאַחַר כָּךְ נִגְנַז אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
But afterward the first light was hidden;
וְלָכֵן חָשְׁבוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג יא, ב)
and therefore the holy Zohar (Zohar III 11b) counts
"Let there be light" as the first utterance
And this is why we say afterward,
"and the table with bread to the north, etc.":
we mention it with the word "shulchan,"
which is in the Holy Tongue,
which alludes to the Written Torah;
which is the "back side" of the Holy Tongue,
And the main founding of the Oral Torah
"Ezra came up from Bavel and established it, etc.;
Rabbi Chiya and his sons established it."
its letters are counted and numbered;
therefore we say "with a new table"
אַף שֶׁהָיָה שָׁרְשׁוֹ גַּם בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
although his root was also in the Written Torah,
and the genealogy of Divrei HaYamim";
שֶׁתִּנָּתֵן תּוֹרָה עַל יָדוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כוּלֵּי
that the Torah be given to Yisrael through him, etc.;
the script was changed through him, etc."
Ezra was of the Men of the Great Assembly,
שֶׁהֵם הִתְחִילוּ לְפַשֵּׁט הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
who began to spread the Oral Torah,
we call it the Oral Torah"
is the time in which to rectify the eating,
